utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the first case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case IT-97-25-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Appearances, please. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The Prosecution is represented today by Ms. Peggy Kuo and my name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. For Mr. Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence will be represented by Mr. Miroslav Vasic, Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krnojelac, are you able to hear the proceedings in a language which you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not Kunarac. I'm Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Judge Hunt, interpreter's lapsus linguae.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I thought I said Krnojelac. I may not have pronounced it correctly. Are you able to hear the proceedings in a language which you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Please sit down. The interpreter has conceded that it was her error and not mine, and I'm grateful for that. If there's one person I think I should be able to recognise at this stage, it would be Mr. Kunarac. Now this is a Status Conference in accordance with Rule 65 bis. Is there anything which is to be raised under the terms of that Rule, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has no questions to discuss. The accused is just interested in indications about the trial date, if there are any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. Vasic. That's, indeed, what we are interested in. Now, from the Prosecution's point of view, what stage have we reached? At the last Status Conference, the accused had not at that stage been interviewed. Has he been interviewed yet?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. During the last two months we have conducted several interviews. The last one was actually yesterday. Because of the health reasons, we had to interrupt our interviews we had some weeks ago. The last interview took place yesterday and we are now finished with the interview process. What we need to do now is to have another extensive discussion with Defence counsel about stipulations, if we could find some agreement so that we can shorten the trial and would not need to have all the witnesses here in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You mean you haven't yet got on to the issue of agreed facts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, because we wanted first to have the interview finished, and now we have scheduled already another meeting with Defence counsel, but due to the summer holiday, it will only be on the 22nd of September. During this meeting, which will maybe last also several days, we think we can find an agreement on stipulated facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What about Rule 66? Have you now supplied all of the documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are they redacted or unredacted?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think they are unredacted but I'm not sure -- no, I'm not sure. The originals as the supporting material were redacted but the additional -- the additional materials like statements, they were then given with their names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: When do you propose to disclose the names and other identifying material and supporting material?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think the names are known to the Defence counsel. We can do it right now. I mean, it's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, you should, because I think that the time has come. Whatever view one might take about protective measures, the time has come to disclose all of that material for this trial.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, we can do it right away. The names are known to Defence counsel and he got other unredacted statements of potential witnesses. But I ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure that that's very satisfactory because it means that there may be material in the supporting documents which is not correctly identified or whatever. Just so there can be no argument later on, I suggest that you comply with, I say, a 14-day order to identify all persons named in the supporting material so that we've got it straight, and there can be no argument at the trial that they haven't been given it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we will take care of this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. That order will be made. You say that all of the statements under 66(A)(ii) has, in fact, been supplied in an unredacted form.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that's very good to hear. Have there been any matters to be raised by way of inspection of documents, et cetera, under 66(B)?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The next one is the provisions of Rule 67. Have you notified the Defence of the names of the witnesses you intend to call?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: When will you do that?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We thought this would be part of the pre-trial materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think that we've got to look at it now because hopefully this trial will be able to commence at the very conclusion of Kunarac. It may even be possible, depending on what happens, to start it whilst we're waiting for written submissions from counsel. I see Ms. Kuo shaking her head. I'm not concerned about the problems of the Prosecution having the same counsel in each. Our obligation is made very clear: we have to get on with the next trial. If the Prosecution has set out to put the same counsel in consecutive trials, it's a matter for them to resolve, not me. I'm not saying we're going to do it because there may not be time, but I want to be able to call this case on for hearing as soon as possible and with little notice as possible, and I'll come to the question of notice shortly. However, when do you think you'll be in a position to be able to notify the names of the witnesses you intend to call?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can do it on short notice, actually, because there's no doubt about who will come. It will be the detainees who can say something about Mr. Krnojelac's position and about the conditions, and the names of these detainees are known to Defence counsel and also the statements are already in his possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The Defence counsel can only guess at what the intention of the Prosecutor is. And the Rule is very firmly stated, "as early as reasonably practicable" you must notify the names of the witnesses the Prosecutor intends to call. Now --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What we can do is we can do this within 14 days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Well, then, an order will be made along those lines. I should say, if only because of an issue which arose in Brdjanin and Talic, that although that Rule and 67(A)(ii) speak about an intention, if the Prosecutor forms an intention to call a particular witness at a very late stage, and only then provides the statement and notifies of that intention, it may be that that witness will not be allowed to be called. So I suggest the Prosecution should have very much in mind an open disclosure of its intentions and a speedy formation of those intentions. What about Rule 68? How are you going with that?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We have fulfilled our obligations and we are still doing it. For instance, in the Kunarac case, there came up some material which was provided to the Defence counsel and will be provided to the Defence counsel also in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. The performance of the Prosecution in relation to Rule 68, of course, has been subject to criticism in other cases. That's why I'm very concerned to keep emphasising this continuing nature of the obligation. And it may be that we will require another signed report by somebody that they have made full investigation of that matter at some time prior to the trial. Have you received a notice of any special plea yet? I should imagine not yet from the state of progress so far.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, of course, the Defence doesn't have to notify that until they've received a compliance with Rule 67(A)(i). The fixing of times of pre-trial briefs is probably a little premature, but I would expect the Prosecution to start thinking of a time when that will be ready so that there should be a very speedy compliance with the terms of Rule 65 ter. I also want to indicate that we propose in this case to vary slightly the way in which documents are tendered. The present system, which is better, I hasten to add, than it is in other Chambers nevertheless does cause some confusion as to whether a document is, in fact, in evidence. What I suggest is that the Prosecution should continue to prenumber its documents but not to call them an exhibit. They can be marked as an exhibit if they, in fact, become an exhibit. But they can be prenumbered and that is the number that can be used to identify them, they being marked for identification, and it will also be the number of them as an exhibit if they become an exhibit. But they should not be called an exhibit until they become one. That, I think, will prevent an awful lot of confusion. The next thing I wanted to ask: What sort of notice does each party require as to the precise date for commencing the trial?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I must confess that we have not considered this but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you could give it some consideration. It's a very important matter. The state of the list is such that we would be subject to, I think, a justifiable criticism if we did not start this as soon as possible after the current trial. The current trial, of course, is in the hands of the Defence at the moment and we simply do not know how long it's going to take. But at some stage during the course of the Kunarac trial, it will become apparent, when the evidence will finish, and at that stage I would like to be able to notify the parties here in this case of a date when we hope to be able to commence the trial. Now, that should not be a very long period. I'm talking about a matter of weeks rather than anything else. So if you could give some consideration to what time you need to notify your first lot of witnesses and that sort of thing, then we'll be in a position to be able to fix a date. Now, Mr. Vasic, from your point of view, what sort of notice do you require or does Mr. Bakrac require for the commencement of the trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence will be ready to commence the trial as soon as you have finished the ongoing trial, and the Defence will make no problems in requiring additional time for preparing the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You mean you'll be able to fit in with whatever date we fix at that stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, during this period of waiting for the trial, the Defence has been preparing for our trial without knowing when it will actually begin. So the Defence will be in a position to accept whatever date you set.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm very grateful to hear that. I should say so that everybody knows at this stage, the Trial Chamber will not be able to sit during those first two weeks of December, that the term continues because of home-leave for some of our members. If we can start the trial in the end of this year, we will certainly start it if we can get a good substantial run-on. Otherwise it may, unfortunately, be the beginning of next year. But we do not propose to lose the idea of starting it hopefully before the end of November.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have just discussed it with my colleague. What we need for the preparation of the witnesses, and especially for the travel arrangements and the discussions with the Victims and Witnesses Unit, we would need three weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Three weeks.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Three weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's a good figure. I'm quite happy with that. Is there anything else that either party wishes to raise in this Status Conference? Very well, then. We'll adjourn, and hopefully there will not be the need for another Status Conference and we'll see you at the beginning of the Pre-Trial Conference. We're adjourned now.
